FINDING 4 — VALID program rejected: a function body with ~396+ statements is
refused with a parse error.

FILE: parse_stmt_count_cap_overrejects.zen.txt — `main` with 400 plain local
      declarations (`x0: i32 := 0` … `x399: i32 := 399`) and a println.
CMD:  ./zen check tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/parse_stmt_count_cap_overrejects.zen.txt
OUT:  zenc: <file>: error[parse]: syntax error: unparseable top-level input
      hint: check the syntax around this top-level declaration
      rc 1                       (no line, no column, no caret)

THRESHOLD: 395 statements -> `ok`;  400 statements -> the error above.

CAUSE: src/compiler/parse_stmt.zen:203 runs the STATEMENT LIST through
      pdepth_enter/pdepth_over, i.e. one statement costs one unit of the same
      PARSE_DEPTH_CAP = 400 budget that bounds nesting
      (src/compiler/parse_type.zen:106). A statement list is not nesting: 400
      consecutive statements in one function is ordinary code, so the comment
      at parse_type.zen:104 — "orders of magnitude above any real program's
      nesting, so it never over-rejects" — does not hold for this path.

CLASS: compiler over-rejection of valid Zen, plus a positionless diagnostic.
FOUND BY: hand-directed probing (a 5000-declaration generated program).
